page: Microsoft Azure D64ds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.8 GHz. It delivers 64 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU subsystem includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AVX, AVX-512 (including AVX512_VNNI), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic primitives. Memory capacity totals 256 GB, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 4 GB per virtual core.

Local ephemeral storage is bundled with the instance, providing 2577 GB of solid-state disk (SSD) space for temporary caching, swap, or scratch data. The server does not incorporate hardware accelerators or dedicated GPUs, and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Network and I/O subsystems support high-throughput operations, matching the scale of its 64-vCPU architecture.

Benchmark data demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded compute and memory bandwidth characteristics, contrasted with moderate single-threaded performance. The instance achieved top-quartile results in multi-core metrics, including a PassMark CPU score of 61088.87, a Geekbench multi-core score of 16347.0, and 41984.0 in Clang compilation tests. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 291.37 GB/sec, accompanied by 132.39 GB/sec write bandwidth. Database operations and key-value caching showed strong execution rates, registering 30451.83 in PassMark database operations and 62.19 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. Web throughput reached 52.02 GB/sec.

Tradeoffs center on single-thread responsiveness and larger neural model execution. Single-core evaluations placed the host in the middle 50% bracket across Geekbench (1657.0) and stress-ng (1899.28). Text generation tasks on large 70-billion-parameter language models scored in the lowest quartile at 2.72 tokens per second due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware. D64ds_v5 offers balanced compute density and local SSD space for relational databases, Redis caching layers, Clang build farms, and multi-threaded enterprise services.
description: Microsoft Azure D64ds_v5 is a general-purpose instance featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. Equipped with 256 GB of memory and 2577 GB of bundled local SSD storage, the instance maintains a balanced 1:4 CPU-to-RAM ratio without discrete GPU acceleration. Benchmark measurements highlight top-quartile performance in multi-threaded execution, memory throughput, and database operations, including a PassMark CPU score of 61088.87 and Redis throughput exceeding 62 million operations per second. Single-core processing aligns with median performance ranges, and generative text tasks on larger parameter models remain limited by CPU inference constraints. D64ds_v5 is suited for large-scale enterprise web backends, software compilation pipelines, distributed caching clusters, and relational database management systems.
